category_title: At-risk students with learning disabilities who are shy and struggle to articulate ideas from print text
minimal_context: The student is working independently to complete two short writing assignments based on a text read in class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please complete these two short writing assignments based on the text we just finished.

STUDENT: I felt confused by the poem at first and then we reread it and I understood it a little better, but I don't know what to write.

TUTOR: Just write down what you remember about the historical events we discussed.

STUDENT: I have a lot of confusion about why Jews were targeted, hated and segregated in Germany at the time of the Third Reich. I can't explain it.

TUTOR: Try your best to put your thoughts on the paper for the assignment.

STUDENT: Writing assignments are more difficult because you have to remember all the information and then put it how you want to say it on paper. But it doesn’t always come out how you want it to.

options.A: Allow the student to choose their own creative projects based on their strengths and interests.
options.B: Maintain a ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 during the writing assignments.
options.C: Implement cross-age and same-age peer tutoring to assist the student with the writing assignments.
options.D: Provide noncontingent attention throughout the day and ignore problem behaviors that function to gain attention.
